subject: Insurance
title: Japan's Mandatory and Voluntary Layers
description: A quick, practical guide to Japan's Mandatory and Voluntary Layers.

hook.text: Japan has two auto insurance layers: compulsory JBAI covers injury to others.

buildup.text: JBAI—Japan's compulsory auto insurance—covers only bodily injury to third parties.

discovery.text: About 88% of Japanese drivers add voluntary insurance for property damage, collision, and higher liability limits.

twist.text: Japan's claim frequency is the lowest among major nations.

climax.text: Japan's dual-layer system combines a government-mandated floor with voluntary market competition.

punchline.text: Two layers: mandatory plus voluntary. Japan's system achieves 88% full coverage.

quiz.question: What does Japan's compulsory JBAI auto insurance cover?
options: Only bodily injury to third parties
